a: PostgreSQL is a powerful open-source relational database.
SQLite is a file-based SQL database good for small apps and tests.
Redis is an in-memory store used for cache, queues, and sessions.
Migrations version schema changes in a controlled way.
Pools reuse DB connections to avoid open/close overhead.
ORMs map tables to objects; still learn SQL for hard queries.
Regular backups and restore tests protect against data loss.
Indexes speed reads but slow writes and use disk.
N+1 queries fetch a list then one query per row; batch or join instead.
